values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations. 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period.' Not allowed near developed sites (campgrounds, picnic areas, trailheads); keep the campsite within 150 ft of the road.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins ('Recreationist can camp anywhere in the National Forest outside a designated campground'; 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period'; 'Dispersed camping is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads ... Keep your campsite within 150 feet from a roadway'), read 2026-10-21

summary: No Forest Service page names Oronoco (fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/oronoco* all 404; not on recreation.gov). Applied the forest's dispersed-camping rules from its camping page: not reservable, first-come, 14 days in any 30. Fees ($0) and note left as they are.
flags: Website is an aggregator/blog (tmbtent.com 'virginia-free-dispersed-camping'), not an agency page; the George Washington & Jefferson NF has no page for Oronoco. Nearest official page is the forest's dispersed-camping page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins.

Possible change of status: Modern Campground reported on 2023-10-01 (https://moderncampground.com/?p=39932) that the forest proposed a $14 fee for Oronoco, 'a previously free dispersed camping spot', with potable water and delineated campsites. No official page confirms whether it was adopted; if it was, the $0 fees and dispersed rules are stale. Worth a call to the Glenwood-Pedlar district.
Inclusion evidence rests on Campendium (vault toilets, '~a dozen RVs of any size'); nothing official confirms RV fit or facilities.
